newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Bond market unease seen bar to Portugal rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Bond market unease seen bar to Portugal rate cut.

text.p: Rising yields across southern European bond markets -- prompted by sudden unease over Spain and Italy's chances of joining EMU -- make a repo rate cut by the Bank of Portugal on Friday unlikely, traders and analysts said.

Although the Bank has room, theoretically, to lower its 7.10 percent repo rate, the uncertainty unleashed by negative statements from German central bankers on Italy and Spain's prospects point to a cautious approach by the Bank, they said.
Reuters polled five analysts and traders and they all ruled out any change when the Bank of Portugal announces on Friday conditions for the next commercial reserve period.
"It is unlikely that the Bank of Portugal will do anything this week...because today and yesterday the (bond) market has been under pressure," said one money market trader.
The Bank has cut its key money market rate 140 basis points since the start of the year.
